title: Factors driving misinformation production and user engagement with toothache content on Facebook
screen_reason: Cross-sectional infodemiology content analysis of 500 Portuguese-language toothache Facebook posts; reports the share of posts containing misinformation (39.6%, n = 198) with an explicit denominator, coded by two trained investigators against current scientific evidence/guidelines. This is a CONTENT prevalence estimate.

estimates.country: Portuguese-language posts; authors from native Portuguese-speaking countries (study framed around Brazil)
estimates.date: posts published between August 2018 and August 2022 (dataset downloaded 26 October 2022)
estimates.measure_type: % of toothache-related Portuguese-language Facebook posts that contained misinformation
estimates.value_raw: 39.6% of posts (n = 198) contained misinformation, out of 500 posts analysed
estimates.denominator: 500 Portuguese-language toothache-related Facebook posts (the 500 with the highest total user interaction, drawn from 899 retrieved posts within a 10,000-post CrowdTangle download)
estimates.definition: A post was coded as containing misinformation only if it unequivocally presented false or misleading information with potential to harm users, judged against current scientific evidence (guidelines, consensus statements and systematic reviews on toothache management)
estimates.misinfo_def: 'Misinformation' was defined as an overarching term encompassing content that is either false or misleading, irrespective of any intent to deceive or cause harm
estimates.source_quote: The results reveal that 39.6% of posts ( n = 198) contained misinformation.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract (Results); repeated in Discussion, p. 7 ('The results reveal that 39.6% of posts (n = 198) contained misinformation.')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent trained and calibrated investigators (TSM, MMM) coded facticity against current scientific evidence, including guidelines, consensus statements and systematic reviews on toothache management; calibration on 50 randomly selected posts until ICC > 0.7, achieved ICC range 0.710-1.000; disagreements resolved by joint review and consensus
estimates.moderator_quote: In the search process for relevant publications, keywords related to toothache were inserted, using associations with Boolean terms and hashtags in Portuguese, through the CrowdTangle search bar... On October 26, 2022, we downloaded a dataset containing 10,000 posts in Portuguese published between August 2018 and August 2022... To ensure we include the most relevant posts, we classify posts based on total user interaction... For in-depth qualitative analysis, a sample size of 500 posts with the highest total interaction was determined according to previous studies.
estimates.notes: Single-issue (toothache) keyword corpus -> denom_scope topical; the sample is the top 500 posts by total interaction, hence denom_selection=curated (engagement-truncated, not random). Country is a JUDGEMENT CALL: the sample is defined by language (Portuguese) with authors from native Portuguese-speaking countries, never enumerated, so coded Global; the paper's framing and its discussion of national statistics point to Brazil, and an adjudicator may prefer country_norm=Brazil. Year coded 2022 (download/end of window); the collection window spans August 2018-August 2022.

missed_or_uncertain: Table 1 reports the distribution of post characteristics (time of publication 50/50, non-financial 369 (73.8%) vs financial 131 (26.2%), regular users 352 (70.4%) vs business/health 148 (29.6%), noncommercial 462 (92.4%) vs commercial 38 (7.6%), negative/neutral 300 (60.0%) vs positive 200 (40.0%), photo/status 356 (71.2%) vs link/video 144 (28.8%)) - these are shares of post attributes, not shares of misinformation, so no rows. Table 2 reports GSEM odds ratios (e.g. misinformation associated with financial motivation OR = 4.38) - associations, not prevalence shares. The flowchart exclusion counts (39 not related to toothache, 5 non-native-Portuguese authors, 7 inaccessible links, 348 repeats) are screening counts, not misinformation. No breakdown of the 39.6% by author profile or format is given as a share, so no sub-rows were invented.

rob.design: Cross-sectional infodemiology (content analysis), STROBE-reported. CrowdTangle keyword search for Portuguese toothache terms; 10,000 posts published Aug 2018-Aug 2022 downloaded 26 Oct 2022; 899 Portuguese posts screened, exclusions for off-topic (39), non-native-Portuguese-country authors (5), inaccessible links (7) and duplicates (348), leaving the top 500 by total interaction. Two independent trained investigators coded facticity, motivation, author profile, content, sentiment and format; calibration on 50 posts to ICC > 0.7, achieved ICC 0.710-1.000; disagreements resolved by consensus. No sampling of a random or complete platform population (engagement-ranked selection); no response-rate concept.
rob.item6_quote: A post was considered to contain misinformation only if it unequivocally presented false or misleading information with the potential to harm Facebook users.
rob.item10_quote: The results reveal that 39.6% of posts (n = 198) contained misinformation.
